claim: Brn3a is expressed in the vast majority of DRG and trigeminal ganglion neurons beginning at approximately E11.
source: Brn3a, a POU-domain transcription factor, is expressed in the vast majority of DRG and trigeminal ganglion neurons beginning at ∼E11 (Fedtsova and Turner, 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fedtsova and Turner, 1995.

claim: The Brn3aCKOAP allele contains one loxP site in the 5′ untranslated region, a second loxP site 3′ of the 3′ UTR, and an alkaline phosphatase reporter distal to the second loxP site.
source: Neurons expressing Brn3a can be visualized using a Brn3a conditional knockout allele (Brn3aCKOAP) that has one loxP site in the 5′ untranslated region (UTR), a second loxP site 3′ of the 3′ UTR, and an alkaline phosphatase (AP) reporter distal to the second loxP site (Badea et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Badea et al., 2009.

claim: Cre-mediated excision of the Brn3a coding region and 3′ UTR activates expression of AP by placing it under the control of the Brn3a promoter.
source: Cre-mediated excision of the Brn3a coding region and 3′ UTR activates expression of AP by placing it under the control of the Brn3a promoter.
evidence: This is a mechanistic description of how the genetic system works, based on established knowledge of Cre-lox recombination systems.

claim: Sparse Cre-mediated recombination was obtained using a Neurofilament Light Chain (NFL)-IRES-CreER knock-in allele and low dose Tamoxifen.
source: In the present study, sparse Cre-mediated recombination was obtained using a Neurofilament Light Chain (NFL)-IRES-CreER knock-in allele and low dose Tamoxifen (Rotolo et al., 2008; see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Rotolo et al., 2008 and reference to the Materials and methods section.

claim: NFL-IRES-CreER is widely expressed in projection neurons and not expressed in non-neural tissue.
source: NFL-IRES-CreER was chosen as the source of Cre-recombinase because it is widely expressed in projection neurons, it is not expressed in non-neural tissue, and it produces a relatively low level of CreER.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the experimental design choice.

claim: Brn3a+/− and Brn3a+/+ mice appear to be indistinguishable in appearance and overall health.
source: Brn3a+/− and Brn3a+/+ mice appear to be indistinguishable in appearance and overall health and individual Brn3a+/− DRG neuronal cell bodies do not differ in appearance or number relative to Brn3a+/+ controls (Xiang et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Xiang et al., 1996.

claim: In Brn3a+/− DRG neurons, a Brn3a-dependent negative feedback regulatory system leads to nearly wild type levels of Brn3a transcripts and other Brn3a-regulated transcripts.
source: Importantly, Trieu et al. (2003) and Eng et al. (2004) have shown that, in Brn3a+/− DRG neurons, a Brn3a-dependent negative feedback regulatory system leads to nearly wild type levels of Brn3a transcripts and other Brn3a-regulated transcripts.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Trieu et al., 2003 and Eng et al., 2004.

claim: Brn3a+/− DRG neurons are unlikely to differ functionally or morphologically from their wild type counterparts.
source: Thus, it seems unlikely that Brn3a+/− DRG neurons differ functionally or morphologically from their wild type counterparts.
evidence: This is an inference based on the previous claim about transcript levels.

claim: The survey of afferent arbor morphologies was conducted with back skin because this territory includes a wide variety of cutaneous sensory types and its large area facilitates the identification of well-isolated AP-stained arbors.
source: The present survey of afferent arbor morphologies was conducted with back skin because this territory includes a wide variety of cutaneous sensory types and its large area facilitates the identification of well-isolated AP-stained arbors.
evidence: This is stated as a rationale for the experimental design choice.

claim: In mature pigmented mice, melanin in skin and hair confounds full-thickness skin imaging.
source: In mature pigmented mice, melanin in skin and hair confounds full-thickness skin imaging.
evidence: This is stated as a technical challenge based on knowledge of melanin's optical properties.

claim: The skin was harvested at P21, the midpoint of the approximately 2-day telogen phase of the highly synchronous first hair cycle.
source: This difficulty was circumvented by harvesting the skin at P21, the midpoint of the ∼2-day telogen phase of the highly synchronous first hair cycle
evidence: This is stated as an experimental design choice to avoid melanin interference.

claim: At P21, back skin pigmentation is at its nadir.
source: Figure 1A shows shaved back skin at P16, P21, and P27 shows the nadir of pigmentation at P21.
evidence: This is demonstrated by visual comparison in Figure 1A.

claim: A total of 101 P21 Brn3aCKOAP/+; NFL-IRES-CreER/+ back skins were analyzed following maternal exposure to 100, 200, 250, or 500 μg of Tamoxifen at GD17.
source: A total of 101 P21 Brn3aCKOAP/+; NFL-IRES-CreER/+ back skins were analyzed following maternal exposure to 100, 200, 250, or 500 μg of Tamoxifen at GD17.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental sample size and conditions.

claim: The average surface area per back skin was 15.53 cm2.
source: With an average surface area of 15.53 cm2 per skin, this corresponds to a total of 1569 cm2 examined for AP stained sensory arbors.
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: A total of 1569 cm2 of back skin was examined for AP stained sensory arbors.
source: With an average surface area of 15.53 cm2 per skin, this corresponds to a total of 1569 cm2 examined for AP stained sensory arbors.
evidence: This is calculated from the number of skins and average area per skin.

claim: The fraction of back skin surface area occupied by well-separated AP+ sensory arbors varied from approximately 0.2% to approximately 15%.
source: The fraction of back skin surface area occupied by well-separated AP+ sensory arbors varied from ∼0.2% to ∼15%.
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: A total of 719 arbors that appeared by visual inspection to be free from overlap were characterized further.
source: A total of 719 arbors that appeared by visual inspection to be free from overlap were characterized further (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sample size for detailed analysis.

claim: 77 full arbors for nine different arbor types were traced using Neuromantic.
source: To analyze arbor morphologies in detail, we traced 77 full arbors for nine different arbor types (Figure 1D) using Neuromantic, a publicly available reconstruction program.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sample size for tracing analysis.

claim: The set of labeled sensory neurons corresponds to the intersection of the expression domains of the Brn3a and NFL genes.
source: The set of labeled sensory neurons is predicted to correspond to the intersection of the expression domains of the Brn3a and NFL genes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genetic labeling strategy used.

claim: Brn3aCKOAP is expressed in nearly all DRG neurons.
source: Although Brn3aCKOAP is expressed in nearly all DRG neurons (Badea et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Badea et al., 2012.

claim: Expression of the NFL-IRES-CreER knock-in allele is enriched in sensory neurons with large axon diameters.
source: expression of the NFL-IRES-CreER knock-in allele presumably mirrors the abundance of the neurofilament light chain and is therefore enriched in sensory neurons with large axon diameters.
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of neurofilament light chain expression patterns.

claim: The current survey likely covers only a fraction of the morphologic diversity of cutaneous sensory arbors.
source: Thus the current survey likely covers only a fraction of the morphologic diversity of cutaneous sensory arbors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of the labeling strategy.

claim: Larger arbors tend to be under-represented because the probability of arbor overlap increases with size.
source: (2) larger arbors tend to be under-represented because the probability of arbor overlap increases with size
evidence: This is an inference about sampling bias based on geometric considerations.

claim: 10 morphologically distinct cutaneous arbor types were identified.
source: Quantitative analyses of 719 arbors, among which 77 were fully reconstructed, reveal 10 morphologically distinct types.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on quantitative analysis of the data.

claim: One arbor type contacts approximately 200 hair follicles with circumferential endings.
source: Among the two types with the largest arbors, one contacts ∼200 hair follicles with circumferential endings
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: One arbor type is characterized by a densely ramifying arbor with one to several thousand branches and a total axon length between one-half and one meter.
source: and a second is characterized by a densely ramifying arbor with one to several thousand branches and a total axon length between one-half and one meter.
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: The smallest afferent arbors appear to target single Merkel cell clusters (touch domes) or single hair follicles.
source: The smallest afferent arbors appear to target single Merkel cell clusters (touch domes) or single hair follicles.
evidence: This is an observation based on visual inspection of the data.

claim: Most of the follicles targeted by I-FACE and I-FALE afferents appear to be guard (tylotrich) hairs based on their large diameter (approximately 50 μm).
source: In the latter category (I-FACE and I-FALE), most of the follicles appear to be guard (tylotrich) hairs based on their large diameter (∼50 μm).
evidence: This is an inference based on morphological measurements.

claim: All cutaneous sensory axons enter the dermis from subdermal nerves and are invariably broken during the skin dissection, generally within several hundred microns of their terminal arbors.
source: The assumption that MCA, I-FACE, and I-FALE afferents target single Merkel clusters or single follicles must be qualified by noting that all cutaneous sensory axons enter the dermis from subdermal nerves and are, therefore, invariably broken during the skin dissection, generally within several hundred microns of their terminal arbors.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical limitations of the dissection method.

claim: An individual axon can innervate more than one Merkel cell cluster based on neurobiotin filling experiments in neonatal mice.
source: This caution is given extra weight by evidence that an individual axon can innervate more than one Merkel cell cluster based on neurobiotin filling experiments in neonatal mice. In these experiments several slowly adapting type I (SAI) low threshold mechanoreceptor axons were observed to innervate two adjacent Merkel cell clusters (Woodbury and Koerber, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Woodbury and Koerber, 2007.

claim: In P21 skin preparations, 20 out of 20 labeled MCA arbors targeted only isolated Merkel cell clusters, with no other labeled MCA arbors seen within a radius of >350 μm.
source: However, in our P21 skin preparations 20/20 labeled MCA arbors targeted only isolated Merkel cell clusters, with no other labeled MCA arbors seen within a radius of >350 μm.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: BE arbors have dense and finely branched processes that encompass an area of 0.5–1 mm in diameter and ramify at a depth of 5–10 μm from the skin surface.
source: A distinct class of arbors, which we refer to as bushy ending (BE), have dense and finely branched processes that encompass an area of 0.5–1 mm in diameter and ramify at a depth of 5–10 μm from the skin surface
evidence: This is a morphological description based on measurements from the data.

claim: BE arbors have a second, deeper arbor that ramifies at a depth of approximately 70 μm from the skin surface.
source: BE arbors have a second, deeper arbor that ramifies at a depth of ∼70 μm from the skin surface
evidence: This is a morphological description based on measurements from the data.

claim: TE arbors have only 20–80 branch points and exhibit relatively sparse coverage of an irregular area of 300–500 μm in diameter at a depth of approximately 20 μm from the skin surface.
source: Another distinctive type of arbor, which we refer to as thick ending (TE), has only 20–80 branch points and exhibits relatively sparse coverage of an irregular area of 300–500 μm in diameter at a depth of ∼20 μm from the skin surface
evidence: This is a morphological description based on measurements from the data.

claim: LD-FALE arbors innervate between 2 and 36 follicles.
source: One type, low-density follicle-associated lanceolate endings (LD-FALE), has a sparsely branched arbor that innervates between 2 and 36 follicles (Figure 4A–D).
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: LD-FALE arbors encompass territories of 1–2 mm in diameter, with total axon lengths of only 5–35 mm and with only 5–40 branch points.
source: These arbors encompass territories of 1–2 mm in diameter, but with total axon lengths of only 5–35 mm and with only 5–40 branch points (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: In nearly every instance, the opening of the 'C' of lanceolate endings faces the anterior of the mouse.
source: In nearly every instance, the opening of the 'C' faces the anterior of the mouse (Figure 8E).
evidence: This is an observation from the data, with quantitative support shown in Figure 8E.

claim: HD-FALE is the most commonly encountered arbor type, accounting for approximately 50% of all AP+ arbors.
source: The most commonly encountered arbor type, high density follicle-associated lanceolate ending (HD-FALE), accounts for ∼50% of all AP+ arbors
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the data.

claim: SA-FACE arbors were rarely observed (8 out of 719 arbors).
source: One type, which we refer to as small area follicle-associated circumferential ending (SA-FACE) was rarely observed (8 out of 719 arbors).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the data.

claim: SA-FACE arbors contact few follicles (mean ± SD of 3.8 ± 1.1), generally have fewer than 20 branch points, and have diameters of approximately 200 to approximately 500 μm.
source: SA-FACE follicles contact few follicles (mean ± SD of 3.8 ± 1.1), generally have fewer than 20 branch points, and have diameters of ∼200 to ∼500 μm
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: LA-FACE arbors contact approximately 200 follicles within territories of approximately 2 mm diameter.
source: LA-FACE arbors contact ∼200 follicles within territories of ∼2 mm diameter
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: LA-FACE arbors have total axon lengths of 100–200 mm and 200–400 branch points.
source: LA-FACE arbors have total axon lengths of 100–200 mm and 200–400 branch points
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: The areas of SA-FACE and LA-FACE arbors are non-overlapping.
source: Figure 8A also shows that the areas of SA-FACE and LA-FACE arbors are non-overlapping.
evidence: This is an observation from the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: LA-FE arbors appear to comprise a single morphologic class and are the largest arbors.
source: The largest arbors appear to comprise a single morphologic class, referred to as large arbors with free endings (LA-FE;
evidence: This is a classification based on morphological analysis of the data.

claim: LA-FE arbors have territories of 3–5 mm diameter.
source: LA-FE arbors have territories of 3–5 mm diameter
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: LA-FE arbors have total axon lengths of 500–1000 mm and 1000–3000 branch points.
source: LA-FE arbors have total axon lengths of 500–1000 mm and 1000–3000 branch points
evidence: This is a measurement reported from the experimental data.

claim: LA-FE arbors have a distinct inner arbor that ramifies at a depth of approximately 70 μm from the skin surface.
source: LA-FE arbors have a distinct inner arbor that ramifies at a depth of ∼70 μm from the skin surface
evidence: This is a morphological description based on measurements from the data.

claim: Each sensory arbor exhibits a high degree of uniformity in its terminal structures.
source: One important result from this survey is that each sensory arbor exhibits a high degree of uniformity in its terminal structures.
evidence: This is a general conclusion drawn from observations across all arbor types.

claim: Arbors with lanceolate endings never produce circular endings, bushy endings, or thick endings.
source: Thus, arbors with lanceolate endings never produce circular endings, bushy endings, or thick endings
evidence: This is an observation from the data across all traced arbors.

claim: Arbors with circular endings never produce lanceolate endings, bushy endings, or thick endings.
source: arbors with circular endings never produce lanceolate endings, bushy endings, or thick endings
evidence: This is an observation from the data across all traced arbors.

claim: The morphologic uniformity of terminal structures within each arbor type argues for a corresponding uniformity in the sensory transduction apparatus.
source: The morphologic uniformity of terminal structures—presumably the sites of transduction of the sensory stimulus—within each arbor type argues for a corresponding uniformity in the sensory transduction apparatus and, consequently, in the range and types of favored stimuli.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed morphological uniformity.

claim: Cutaneous sensory afferents represent a set of labeled lines, collectively delivering to the dorsal spinal cord at least 10 parallel representations of external stimuli that impinge on hairy skin.
source: Thus, these data support the view that cutaneous sensory afferents represent a set of labeled lines, collectively delivering to the dorsal spinal cord at least 10 parallel representations of external stimuli that impinge on hairy skin.
evidence: This is an inference based on the morphological diversity and uniformity within types.

claim: MCA arbors likely correspond to the A-beta slowly adapting type I/low threshold mechanoreceptors (SA I/SA LTMRs) that contact Merkel cell clusters/touch domes.
source: MCA arbors likely correspond to the A-beta slowly adapting type I/low threshold mechanoreceptors (SA I/SA LTMRs) that contact Merkel cell clusters/touch domes.
evidence: This is an inference based on known properties of Merkel cell-associated neurons.

claim: I-FALE arbors that surround guard hair follicles likely correspond to A-beta rapidly adapting (RA) LTMRs.
source: I-FALE arbors that surround guard hair follicles likely correspond to A-beta rapidly adapting (RA) LTMRs.
evidence: This is an inference based on known properties of guard hair follicle-associated neurons.

claim: HD-FALE arbors likely correspond to A-beta RA LTMRs that innervate awl/auchenne hair follicles.
source: HD-FALE arbors likely correspond to A-beta RA LTMRs that innervate awl/auchenne hair follicles.
evidence: This is an inference based on known properties of awl/auchenne hair follicle-associated neurons.

claim: I-FACE, LA-FACE, and SA-FACE arbors likely correspond to the peptidergic and/or nonpeptidergic circumferential free nerve endings described by Fundin et al. (1997).
source: I-FACE, LA-FACE, and SA-FACE arbors likely correspond to the peptidergic and/or nonpeptidergic circumferential free nerve endings described by Fundin et al. (1997)
evidence: This is an inference based on morphological similarity to previously described structures, supported by citation.

claim: TE arbors could correspond to the thickened endings of myelinated fibers referred to by Rice and colleagues as 'fuzzy endings' or 'club endings', which are suggested to represent mechanoreceptors.
source: TE arbors could correspond to the thickened endings of myelinated fibers referred to by Rice and colleagues as 'fuzzy endings' or 'club endings', which are suggested to represent mechanoreceptors (Fundin et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on morphological similarity, supported by citation.

claim: BE and LA-FE arbors come close to and may partially penetrate the epidermis.
source: The two types of arbors with free endings—BE and LA-FE arbors—come close to and may partially penetrate the epidermis (Figure 8D)
evidence: This is an observation from depth measurements shown in Figure 8D.

claim: BE arbors bear a particularly close resemblance to the arbors of MrgprB4-expressing neurons.
source: BE arbors bear a particularly close resemblance to the arbors of MrgprB4-expressing neurons, one of a large number of Mrgpr-expressing neurons that together mediate the sense of itch (Liu et al., 2007, 2009).
evidence: This is an inference based on morphological similarity, supported by citations.

claim: I-FALE and I-FACE arbors that target single guard hair follicles are predicted to gather sensory information at single follicle resolution with a sampling pattern based on the regular mosaic of guard hairs.
source: For those I-FALE and I-FACE arbors that target single guard hair follicles, the clear prediction is that sensory information is gathered at single follicle resolution with a sampling pattern based on the regular mosaic of guard hairs.
evidence: This is an inference about function based on the observed morphology.

claim: LA-FE neurons are predicted to have receptive fields of 3–5 mm diameter with dense and relatively homogeneous coverage by sensory endings.
source: At the opposite extreme, LA-FE neurons are predicted to have receptive fields of 3–5 mm diameter with dense and relatively homogeneous coverage by sensory endings.
evidence: This is an inference about function based on the observed morphology.

claim: BE neurons are predicted to have receptive fields of 0.5–1 mm diameter with an even higher density of sensory endings than LA-FE neurons.
source: BE neurons are predicted to have receptive fields of 0.5–1 mm diameter with an even higher density of sensory endings.
evidence: This is an inference about function based on the observed morphology.

claim: Spatial resolution is predicted to be relatively low for HD-FALE arbors, each of which contacts most follicles within its approximately 0.5 to approximately 1 mm diameter territory.
source: Spatial resolution is also predicted to be relatively low for HD-FALE arbors, each of which contacts most follicles within its ∼0.5 to ∼1 mm diameter territory
evidence: This is an inference about function based on the observed morphology.

claim: HD-FALE arbors presumably sense hair deflections.
source: these afferents presumably sense hair deflections.
evidence: This is an inference about function based on the morphology and known properties of lanceolate endings.

claim: Two or three HD-FALE arbors might co-innervate a single follicle.
source: Many HD-FALE endings cover only part of the circumference of their associated follicle, suggesting that two or three HD-FALE arbors might co-innervate a single follicle
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed partial coverage of follicles.

claim: Deflection of a single hair might elicit synchronous responses in several HD-FALE arbors.
source: and, therefore, that deflection of a single hair might elicit synchronous responses in several HD-FALE arbors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proposed co-innervation pattern.

claim: For any given HD-FALE and LD-FALE arbor, the C-shaped territories of different lanceolate clusters generally reside on the same side of their associated follicles.
source: For any given HD-FALE and LD-FALE arbor, the C-shaped territories of different lanceolate clusters generally reside on the same side of their associated follicles (Figures 4A–C and 8E).
evidence: This is an observation from the data, with quantitative support shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The asymmetric localization of lanceolate endings suggests a corresponding asymmetry in mechanosensory responses.
source: This asymmetric localization suggests a corresponding asymmetry in mechanosensory responses.
evidence: This is an inference about function based on the observed structural asymmetry.

claim: If hair deflection toward a lanceolate ending elicits a response opposite to that of hair deflection away from the lanceolate ending, then the asymmetric locations of lanceolate endings would provide information about the direction of hair movement.
source: By analogy with the responses of auditory and vestibular sensory cells, if hair deflection toward a lanceolate ending ('compression') elicits a response opposite to that of hair deflection away from the lanceolate ending ('extension'), then the asymmetric locations of lanceolate endings would necessarily provide information about the direction of hair movement.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on analogy with other sensory systems.

claim: A coherent wave of mechanical stimulation would presumably elicit a response of the same polarity from multiple similarly oriented C-shaped endings.
source: A coherent wave of mechanical stimulation—the sort delivered by a large object moving over the body surface—would presumably elicit a response of the same polarity from multiple similarly oriented C-shaped endings.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about function based on the observed structural organization.

claim: The innervated follicles in LD-FALE arbors are spaced at large intervals (approximately 0.5 mm).
source: The pattern of spatially asymmetric C-shaped lanceolate clusters is especially striking among LD-FALE arbors because the innervated follicles are spaced at large intervals (∼0.5 mm)
evidence: This is a measurement from the data.

claim: If LD-FALE neurons sense coherent hair deflections with low spatial resolution, then these neurons would represent excellent candidates for the C-fiber neurons that subserve affective touch stimuli of the sort elicited by a mother licking her pups.
source: If, as seems probable, the LD-FALE neurons sense coherent hair deflections with low spatial resolution, then these neurons would represent excellent candidates for the C-fiber neurons that subserve affective touch stimuli of the sort elicited by a mother licking her pups (Andrew, 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative inference about function, supported by citation.

claim: Similar C-fiber responses to low force, slowly moving stimuli—referred to as 'pleasant touch'—have been recorded from human hairy skin by microneurography.
source: Similar C-fiber responses to low force, slowly moving stimuli—referred to as 'pleasant touch'—have also been recorded from human hairy skin by microneurography (Johansson et al., 1988; Löken et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Johansson et al., 1988 and Löken et al., 2009.

claim: LA-FACE arbors show a pattern of dense follicle coverage, with approximately 60% of follicles contacted in a territory of approximately 2 mm diameter.
source: A pattern of dense follicle coverage is seen in LA-FACE arbors, with ∼60% of follicles contacted in a territory of ∼2 mm diameter.
evidence: This is a measurement from the data.

claim: There are clear differences among follicles in the number of AP+ circumferential fibers.
source: Although AP histochemistry cannot resolve individual fibers within a tightly packed circumferential bundle, there are clear differences among follicles in the number of AP+ circumferential fibers
evidence: This is an observation from the data.

claim: Many follicles receive fibers from two or more LA-FACE arbors.
source: If we suppose that each follicle receives roughly the same total number of circumferential fibers, then these data suggest that many follicles receive fibers from two or more LA-FACE arbors
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed variation in staining intensity.

claim: The coverage factor for HD-FALE arbors would be between one and two.
source: If we assume that each follicle's circumference is fully and uniformly occupied by lanceloate endings—an assumption supported by high resolution light and electron microscopic imaging (Casserly et al., 1994; Takahashi-Iwanaga, 2000; Li et al., 2011)—then the coverage factor for HD-FALE arbors would be between one and two.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed innervation patterns, supported by citations.

claim: The coverage factor for LA-FACE arbors is estimated to be 2–4.
source: On the assumption that every follicle receives a level of circumferential fiber coverage that roughly corresponds to the highest levels observed in our samples, and with each LA-FACE arbor encircling ∼60% of follicles within its territory, we estimate a coverage factor of 2–4.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed innervation patterns.

claim: LD-FALE arbors could potentially have coverage factors of >30.
source: Following the same logic, LD-FALE arbors could potentially have coverage factors of >30 since they innervate hair follicles that are spaced at intervals of ∼0.5 mm (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the observed innervation patterns.

claim: The mechanisms that determine laminar specificity, target specificity, and arbor size and branching density among cutaneous afferents are unknown.
source: In particular, the mechanisms that determine laminar specificity, target specificity, and arbor size and branching density among cutaneous afferents are unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Competition among arbors of the same type for a limited pool of targets or target territories could determine the size of individual arbor territories.
source: For sensory arbors that contact multiple follicles, competition among arbors of the same type for a limited pool of targets or target territories—such as the finite circumference of each follicle, around which the lanceolate endings are packed—could determine the size of individual arbor territories.
evidence: This is a speculative inference about developmental mechanisms.

claim: Competition has been described among lanceolate endings that innervate the same guard hair follicle.
source: Competition of this sort has been described among lanceolate endings that innervate the same guard hair follicle (Casserly et al., 1994)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Casserly et al., 1994.

claim: The average arbor territory will correlate inversely with, and be controlled by, the number of DRG neurons of the given class per unit area of skin.
source: This model predicts that the average arbor territory will correlate inversely with, and be controlled by, the number of DRG neurons of the given class per unit area of skin.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the competition model.

claim: Axon length and number of branch points vary over a 1,000-fold range across different arbor types.
source: Finally, axon length and number of branch points, which vary over a 1,000-fold range across different arbor types
evidence: This is a summary of measurements from the data.

claim: Axon length and number of branch points could be controlled by regulating, at the level of gene transcription, the abundances and ratios of various cytoskeletal proteins.
source: axon length and number of branch points, which vary over a 1,000-fold range across different arbor types, could be controlled not only by local extrinsic signals but also by regulating, at the level of gene transcription, the abundances and ratios of various cytoskeletal proteins (Gallo, 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative inference about developmental mechanisms, supported by citation.

claim: Hair follicles and their associated structures—Merkel cell clusters (touch domes), arrector pili muscles, and sebaceous glands—are all polarized with respect to the body axes.
source: Hair follicles and their associated structures—Merkel cell clusters (touch domes), arrector pili muscles, and sebaceous glands—are all polarized with respect to the body axes.
evidence: This is a statement based on established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The anterior-to-posterior angle of the hair follicle is under the control of the planar cell polarity pathway.
source: This is macroscopically apparent in the anterior-to-posterior angle of the hair follicle itself, an organizational feature that is under the control of the planar cell polarity pathway (Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2010.

claim: Each hair follicle could transmit polarity information to its associated lanceolate cluster.
source: It seems reasonable to suppose that each hair follicle could transmit polarity information to its associated lanceolate cluster
evidence: This is a speculative inference about developmental mechanisms.

claim: Experiments with mice lacking planar cell polarity signaling in the skin support the conjecture that hair follicles transmit polarity information to lanceolate clusters.
source: and recent experiments with mice lacking planar cell polarity signaling in the skin support this conjecture (Chang and Nathans, unpublished observations).
evidence: This is supported by unpublished data from Chang and Nathans.

claim: The cutaneous sensory system has primary sensory neurons that are abundant, large, and anatomically segregated in the DRG.
source: First, the primary sensory neurons are abundant, large, and anatomically segregated (in the DRG) where they can be studied or dissected either during development or in adulthood.
evidence: This is a statement based on established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The sensory arbors are embedded within a large two-dimensional tissue (the skin) that by virtue of its surface location is readily accessible to controlled stimulation or surgical and pharmacologic manipulations.
source: Second, the sensory arbors are embedded within a large two-dimensional tissue (the skin) that by virtue of its surface location is readily accessible to controlled stimulation or surgical and pharmacologic manipulations.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental advantages of the cutaneous sensory system.

claim: The cutaneous sensory system is the only sensory system in which single unit recordings can be made from primary sensory neurons in an awake human to correlate physiology with psychophysics.
source: And third, it is the only sensory system in which single unit recordings can be made from primary sensory neurons in an awake human to correlate physiology with psychophysics (e.g., Vallbo and Johansson, 1984; Vallbo et al., 1984; Löken et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Vallbo and Johansson, 1984; Vallbo et al., 1984; Löken et al., 2009.

claim: Murine skin is sufficiently thin that intradermal structures can be imaged in their entirety, thus obviating the need for physical sectioning.
